title: fix(app-shell): the Studio package switcher reports its fetch failure instead of swallowing it
body:
Fixes #7368

## The defect, restated as measured on `origin/main` `900f8d995`

`PackageSwitcher` held the package list as `PkgEntry[] | null` and caught the
`fetchPackages()` rejection into an empty block, so `null` meant **both** "still
loading" and "the fetch failed". The trigger rendered `current?.name ?? packageId`,
which collapses a **third** situation into the same pixels: a package whose producer
declared no name at all — `parsePackages` falls `name` back to the id (objectui#7254),
so a loaded-but-nameless row carries the id *as its name*.

All three therefore printed the identical raw reverse-domain id with no toast, no
console line and no retry, forever. The author had no way to tell whether to go fix the
manifest or to go retry.

The `.catch`'s justification is real — navigation still works — but it argues for
**degrading, not for degrading silently**. That distinction is the whole card.

## Call sites, re-measured on `900f8d995` (⚠️ two corrections)

`fetchPackages()` has **four** call sites in the file (the card said three):

| line | where | before | in this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 282 | `PackageSwitcher` load effect | silent `.catch` | **fixed** — report + three-state distinction |
| 343 | `onManageChanged` | silent `catch` | **not touched** — filed as #7821, see below |
| 498 | writability courtesy gate | silent `.catch` | **fixed** — reports |
| 2450 | `DataPillar` namespace lookup | silent `.catch` | **fixed** — reports |

**Correction 1 — `:343` does NOT already report.** The triage comment and the PM ruling
both record that `:343` sits inside the `try` whose `catch` runs `toast.error` at `:329`.
It does not. `:329` is `openManage`'s catch and it wraps `fetchFullPackage`, a different
function; `:343` lives in `onManageChanged`, a separate `useCallback` with its own bare
`catch { /* keep the stale list */ }`. So **all four** sites were swallowing, not three.

**Correction 2 — the `formatMetadataError` count.** The triage measured 10 uses in this
file; on `900f8d995` there are **19** call sites (`grep -o 'formatMetadataError('`, minus
the import), of which 2 reach `toast.error` and the rest reach `setError` / `setAppErr` /
`setCreateErr`. The conclusion the number was drawn for holds either way, and harder: the
switcher was a 19-to-1 exception, not a convention.

`:343` is left alone on purpose — its swallow is not merely silent, it produces a **wrong
decision**, and the honest fix needs a ruling rather than a one-line toast. See the
finding below.

## What changed

- **`:282` — report.** The rejection is formatted with the file's own `formatMetadataError`
  and raised as `toast.error`. The `.catch` stays a `.catch`: ⛔ never a `throw`, so one 503
  still cannot take the Studio top bar down.
- **`:282` — distinguish.** A second state slot (`pkgsErr`) turns the one `null` into three
  named states, derived once as `pkgListState: 'loading' | 'failed' | 'loaded'` and read by
  both the trigger and the popover. A failure wins over a list already in hand, because after
  a failed refresh the names on screen are stale.
  - **loading** — a spinner beside the id.
  - **failed** — a "Failed to load" marker carrying the message on its tooltip, and the
    popover prints the reason instead of reading "Loading…" forever.
  - **loaded** — the id stands alone, where a bare id now really does mean "this package
    declares no name".
  - The trigger also carries `data-pkg-list-state`, which is what the pins read: the trigger's
    *text* is the same string in all three states, so the state cannot be recovered from it.
- **⛔ The id is never replaced.** Per the triage boundary, the states are told apart by what
  stands **next to** the id — swapping it for "Unknown package" would trade the author's one
  diagnostic handle for an uninformative phrase.
- **⛔ No retry.** Per the PM ruling: retry count/backoff/give-up behaviour is undecided, and
  retrying *delays* the moment the failure becomes visible, which is the opposite of the fix.
- **`:498` and `:2450` — report.** Both keep their (correct) fallbacks — ungated writability,
  best-effort namespace — and stop being silent about why the fallback happened.
- **One outage, one toast.** All three report on one shared sonner id
  (`PACKAGE_LIST_TOAST_ID`), so three rejections of the same endpoint on one mount surface as
  a single message. That is the `outcomeToastId` pattern this repo already uses in
  `packages/components/src/renderers/form/form.tsx`.

**No new i18n key.** `engine.studio.loadFailed` ("Failed to load" / 「加载失败」) already exists
and this file already spells the same three-way out at three other empty states
(`error ? loadFailed : loaded ? none : loading`, lines 2856 / 3730 / 4162). The i18n table lives
under `views/metadata-admin/`, which another seat holds — nothing there was touched.

**Clause-② stays `no`:** no new exported symbol or type (`pkgsErr`, `pkgListState` and
`PACKAGE_LIST_TOAST_ID` are all module-private), no published signature change, no new
authorable key, no gate accept/reject set moved.

## Verification — all at `fb68b847f`

Run from the repo root (`pnpm exec vitest run PATHS`), each through this container's shared
heavy-verify lock; exit codes captured by redirecting first, never through a pipe.

| what | result |
|---|---|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/StudioDesignSurface.packageListErrorPosture.test.tsx` | `Test Files 1 passed (1)` · `Tests 7 passed (7)` · VERDICT `command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/` | `Test Files 48 passed (48)` · `Tests 257 passed (257)` · VERDICT `command-exit 0` |
| 10 app-shell tests outside that directory that name `StudioDesignSurface` / `packages-io` / `sonner` | `Test Files 10 passed (10)` · `Tests 122 passed (122)` · VERDICT `command-exit 0` |
| `pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/app-shell --concurrency=2` | `Tasks: 30 successful, 30 total` · VERDICT `command-exit 0` |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | see below |
| `check-changeset-no-major` / `-fixed` / `-overwrite` / `check-control-bytes` | all `✅`, exit 0 |

**Changeset gate, verdict lines quoted verbatim.**

BEFORE (exit 1):

    ❌  1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change adds no changeset:

AFTER (exit 0):

    ✅  1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/7368-studio-package-list-error-posture.md.

**Type-check really covers the new test.** `app-shell`'s `type-check` is
`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`; `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` names both
`StudioDesignSurface.tsx` and the new `.test.tsx` in its program (1 hit each), so "type-check
clean" is a statement about the test file too, not around it.

**Lint adds nothing.** Measured against the `HEAD` blob of the same file linted from the same
directory, so the config is identical: baseline **0 errors / 19 warnings**, this branch **0 errors
/ 19 warnings**, with a byte-identical rule breakdown (`set-state-in-effect` 5,
`exhaustive-deps` 12, `no-unused-vars` 1, `preserve-manual-memoization` 1). The new test file is
0/0. The one `react-hooks/static-components` finding that appears under `--no-inline-config`
is pre-existing (baseline line 2795, here line 2895, same rule, suppressed by an
`eslint-disable-next-line` already in the file) and this package's own lint script is
`eslint .`, which honours it.

**Declared narrowing.** `packages/app-shell` holds 622 test files; the full package does not fit
this container's foreground budget under lock contention. What was run instead is a derived
blast radius — the whole directory containing the changed file (48 files) plus every app-shell
test outside it that names the changed module or its two collaborators (10 files) — measured,
not guessed. The remaining app-shell files are left to CI, which runs the farm exactly once
regardless.

## Ablation — each new guarantee mutated away, on disk, and the pin named itself

Every leg: proved the tree was at `HEAD` first, proved the mutation landed (anchor-count flip to
0 plus a git blob-hash change), ran the pins, restored with `git checkout HEAD -- ABSOLUTE_PATH`
under `trap ... EXIT INT TERM`, and proved restoration **by state** (`git diff HEAD` empty **and**
the file hash back to the `HEAD` blob `c4239c932`).

| leg | guarantee removed | pins that turned red |
|---|---|---|
| A | the report — `.catch` swallows silently again | **5 failed / 2 passed** |
| B | the distinction — `pkgListState` collapses `failed` back into `loading` | **4 failed / 3 passed** |
| C | the shared sonner id on the two sibling sites | **1 failed / 6 passed** — exactly `one outage is one toast` |

No leg was a no-op: each printed `removed-anchor count now 0` and a changed blob hash before the
tests ran, and each printed a matching restore proof after.

## Out of scope, filed not fixed

**#7821 — `onManageChanged` reads a failed refresh as "the package was deleted" and evicts the
author to `/home`.** The fourth `fetchPackages()` call site (`:343`). Its `catch` comment says
"keep the stale list", which is true of the `pkgs` *state* but not of the local `list`, which
stays `[]`. Three lines later `if (!list.some(...))` is therefore always true, the code takes the
**Deleted** branch, and if the managed package is the one under the editor it navigates to
`/home`. A transient 503 after any package lifecycle action silently throws the author out of
the Studio. It is not a one-line toast — what the eviction check should do when the refresh
failed is a ruling — so it is filed rather than ridden along here.
